addons.description: The common chart supports several add-ons. These can be configured under this key.

codeserver.description: The common library supports adding a code-server add-on to access files. It can be configured under this key.

args.description:
Set codeserver command line arguments.
Consider setting --user-data-dir to a persistent location to preserve code-server setting changes

enabled.description: Enable running a code-server container in the pod

env.description: Set any environment variables for code-server here

git.description: Optionally allow access a Git repository by passing in a private SSH key

deployKeyBase64.description: Base64-encoded SSH private key. When both variables are set, the raw SSH key takes precedence.

deployKeySecret.description:
Existing secret containing SSH private key
The chart expects it to be present under the `id_rsa` key.

pullPolicy.description: Specify the code-server image pull policy

enabled.description: Enable an ingress for the code-server add-on.

annotations.description:
Specify the nodePort value for the LoadBalancer and NodePort service types.
ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#type-nodeport
nodePort:

enabled.description: Enable a service for the code-server add-on.

volumeMounts.description:
Specify a list of volumes that get mounted in the code-server container.
At least 1 volumeMount is required!
- name: config
mountPath: /data/config

workingDir.description:
Specify the working dir that will be opened when code-server starts
If not given, the app will default to the mountpah of the first specified volumeMount

netshoot.description:
The common library supports adding a netshoot add-on to troubleshoot network issues within a Pod.
It can be configured under this key.

enabled.description: Enable running a netshoot container in the pod

env.description: Set any environment variables for netshoot here

pullPolicy.description: Specify the netshoot image pull policy

vpn.description: The common chart supports adding a VPN add-on. It can be configured under this key.

args.description: Override the args for the vpn sidecar container

configFile.description:
Provide a customized vpn configuration file to be used by the VPN.
|-
Some Example Config
remote greatvpnhost.com 8888
auth-user-pass
Cipher AES

configFileSecret.description:
Reference an existing secret that contains the VPN configuration file
The chart expects it to be present under the `vpnConfigfile` key.

enabled.description: Enable running a VPN in the pod to route traffic through a VPN

env.description:
All variables specified here will be added to the vpn sidecar container
See the documentation of the VPN image for all config values

gluetun.description:
Make sure to read the [documentation](https://github.com/qdm12/gluetun/wiki)
to see how to configure this addon!

pullPolicy.description: Specify the Gluetun image pull policy

livenessProbe.description:
Optionally specify a livenessProbe, e.g. to check if the connection is still
being protected by the VPN

egress.description:
The egress configuration for your network policy, All outbound traffic
from the pod will be blocked unless specified here.
[[ref]](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/)
[[recipes]](https://github.com/ahmetb/kubernetes-network-policy-recipes)
- to:
- ipBlock:
cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
ports:
- port: 53
protocol: UDP
- port: 53
protocol: TCP

enabled.description:
If set to true, will deploy a network policy that blocks all outbound
traffic except traffic specified as allowed

podSelectorLabels.description: Provide additional podSelector labels which may be required.

scripts.description: Provide custom up/down scripts that can be used by the vpn configuration.

type.description: Specify the VPN type. Valid options are `gluetun`.

args.description: Override the args for the default container

automountServiceAccountToken.description: Specifies whether a service account token should be automatically mounted.

command.description: Override the command(s) for the default container

configMaps.description:
Configure configMaps for the chart here.
Additional configMaps can be added by adding a dictionary key similar to the 'config' object.

annotations.description: Annotations to add to the configMap

data.description: configMap data content. Helm template enabled.

labels.description: Labels to add to the configMap

cronjob.description: CronJob configuration. Required only when using `controller.type: cronjob`.

backoffLimit.description: Limits the number of times a failed job will be retried

concurrencyPolicy.description:
Specifies how to treat concurrent executions of a job that is created by this cron job
valid values are Allow, Forbid or Replace

failedJobsHistory.description: The number of failed Jobs to keep

schedule.description: Sets the CronJob time when to execute your jobs

startingDeadlineSeconds.description: The deadline in seconds for starting the job if it misses its scheduled time for any reason

successfulJobsHistory.description: The number of succesful Jobs to keep

ttlSecondsAfterFinished.description:
If this field is set, ttlSecondsAfterFinished after the Job finishes, it is eligible to
be automatically deleted.

podManagementPolicy.description: Set statefulset podManagementPolicy, valid values are Parallel and OrderedReady (default).

replicas.description: Number of desired pods. When using a HorizontalPodAutoscaler, set this to `null`.

strategy.description:
Set the controller upgrade strategy
For Deployments, valid values are Recreate (default) and RollingUpdate.
For StatefulSets, valid values are OnDelete and RollingUpdate (default).
DaemonSets/CronJobs ignore this.

type.description:
Set the controller type.
Valid options are deployment, daemonset, statefulset or cronjob

dnsConfig.description:
Configuring the ndots option may resolve nslookup issues on some Kubernetes setups.
options:
- name: ndots
value: "1"

dnsPolicy.description:
Defaults to "ClusterFirst" if hostNetwork is false
and "ClusterFirstWithHostNet" if hostNetwork is true.
ClusterFirst

enableServiceLinks.description:
Enable/disable the generation of environment variables for services.
[[ref]](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/connect-applications-service/#accessing-the-service)

env.description:
Main environment variables. Template enabled.
Syntax options:
A) TZ: UTC
B) PASSWD: '{{ .Release.Name }}'
C) PASSWD:
configMapKeyRef:
name: config-map-name
key: key-name
D) PASSWD:
valueFrom:
secretKeyRef:
name: secret-name
key: key-name
...
E) - name: TZ
value: UTC
F) - name: TZ
value: '{{ .Release.Name }}'

envFrom.description:
Secrets and/or ConfigMaps that will be loaded as environment variables.
[[ref]](https://unofficial-kubernetes.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tasks/configure-pod-container/configmap/#use-case-consume-configmap-in-environment-variables)
- configMapRef:
name: config-map-name
- secretRef:
name: secret-name

hostAliases.description:
Use hostAliases to add custom entries to /etc/hosts - mapping IP addresses to hostnames.
[[ref]](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/add-entries-to-pod-etc-hosts-with-host-aliases/)
- ip: "192.168.1.100"
hostnames:
- "example.com"
- "www.example.com"

hostNetwork.description: When using hostNetwork make sure you set dnsPolicy to `ClusterFirstWithHostNet`

ingress.description:
Configure the ingresses for the chart here.
Additional ingresses can be added by adding a dictionary key similar to the 'main' ingress.

hosts.description: Configure the hosts for the ingress

nameOverride.description: Override the name suffix that is used for this ingress.

primary.description:
Make this the primary ingress (used in probes, notes, etc...).
If there is more than 1 ingress, make sure that only 1 ingress is marked as primary.

tls.description:
Configure TLS for the ingress. Both secretName and hosts can process a Helm template.
- secretName: chart-example-tls
hosts:
- chart-example.local

initContainers.description:
Specify any initContainers here as dictionary items.
Each initContainer should have its own key. The dictionary item key will determine the order.
Helm templates can be used.

lifecycle.description: Configure the lifecycle for the main container

persistence.description:
Configure persistence for the chart here.
Additional items can be added by adding a dictionary key similar to the 'config' key.
[[ref]](https://bjw-s.github.io/helm-charts/docs/common-library/common-library-storage)

accessMode.description:
AccessMode for the persistent volume.
Make sure to select an access mode that is supported by your storage provider!
[[ref]](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/#access-modes)

enabled.description: Enables or disables the persistence item

existingClaim.description:
If you want to reuse an existing claim, the name of the existing PVC can be passed here.
your-claim

mountPath.description:
Where to mount the volume in the main container.
Defaults to `/<name_of_the_volume>`,
setting to '-' creates the volume but disables the volumeMount.
/config

nameOverride.description: Override the name suffix that is used for this volume.

readOnly.description: Specify if the volume should be mounted read-only.

retain.description: Set to true to retain the PVC upon `helm uninstall`

size.description: The amount of storage that is requested for the persistent volume.

storageClass.description:
Storage Class for the config volume.
If set to `-`, dynamic provisioning is disabled.
If set to something else, the given storageClass is used.
If undefined (the default) or set to null, no storageClassName spec is set, choosing the default provisioner.
"-"

subPath.description:
Used in conjunction with `existingClaim`. Specifies a sub-path inside the referenced volume instead of its root
some-subpath

type.description:
Sets the persistence type
Valid options are pvc, emptyDir, hostPath, secret, configMap or custom

shared.description:
Create an emptyDir volume to share between all containers
[[ref]]https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#emptydir)

medium.description:
Set the medium to "Memory" to mount a tmpfs (RAM-backed filesystem) instead
of the storage medium that backs the node.
Memory

sizeLimit.description:
If the `SizeMemoryBackedVolumes` feature gate is enabled, you can
specify a size for memory backed volumes.
1Gi

podSecurityContext.description: Configure the Security Context for the Pod

priorityClassName.description:
Custom priority class for different treatment by the scheduler
system-node-critical

custom.description: Set this to `true` if you wish to specify your own livenessProbe

spec.description:
The spec field contains the values for the default livenessProbe.
If you selected `custom: true`, this field holds the definition of the livenessProbe.

custom.description: Set this to `true` if you wish to specify your own readinessProbe

spec.description:
The spec field contains the values for the default readinessProbe.
If you selected `custom: true`, this field holds the definition of the readinessProbe.

custom.description: Set this to `true` if you wish to specify your own startupProbe

spec.description:
The spec field contains the values for the default startupProbe.
If you selected `custom: true`, this field holds the definition of the startupProbe.

periodSeconds.description: This means it has a maximum of 5*30=150 seconds to start up before it fails

resources.description: Set the resource requests / limits for the main container.

route.description:
Configure the gateway routes for the chart here.
Additional routes can be added by adding a dictionary key similar to the 'main' route.
[[ref]](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/references/spec/#gateway.networking.k8s.io%2fv1alpha2)

kind.description:
Set the route kind
Valid options are GRPCRoute, HTTPRoute, TCPRoute, TLSRoute, UDPRoute

nameOverride.description: Override the name suffix that is used for this route.

parentRefs.description: Configure the resource the route attaches to.

rules.description: Configure rules for routing. Defaults to the primary service.

runtimeClassName.description:
Allow specifying a runtimeClassName other than the default one (ie: nvidia)
nvidia

schedulerName.description:
Allows specifying a custom scheduler name
awkward-dangerous-scheduler

secrets.description:
Use this to populate secrets with the values you specify.
Be aware that these values are not encrypted by default, and could therefore visible
to anybody with access to the values.yaml file.
Additional Secrets can be added by adding a dictionary key similar to the 'secret' object.

annotations.description: Annotations to add to the Secret

labels.description: Labels to add to the Secret

stringData.description: Secret stringData content. Helm template enabled.

securityContext.description: Configure the Security Context for the main container

service.description:
Configure the services for the chart here.
Additional services can be added by adding a dictionary key similar to the 'main' service.

ipFamilies.description: The ip families that should be used. Options: IPv4, IPv6

ipFamilyPolicy.description: Specify the ip policy. Options: SingleStack, PreferDualStack, RequireDualStack

nameOverride.description: Override the name suffix that is used for this service

ports.description:
Configure the Service port information here.
Additional ports can be added by adding a dictionary key similar to the 'http' service.

nodePort.description:
Specify the nodePort value for the LoadBalancer and NodePort service types.
[[ref]](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#type-nodeport)

primary.description:
Make this the primary port (used in probes, notes, etc...)
If there is more than 1 service, make sure that only 1 port is marked as primary.

protocol.description:
Port protocol.
Support values are `HTTP`, `HTTPS`, `TCP` and `UDP`.
HTTPS and HTTPS spawn a TCP service and get used for internal URL and name generation

targetPort.description:
Specify a service targetPort if you wish to differ the service port from the application port.
If `targetPort` is specified, this port number is used in the container definition instead of
the `port` value. Therefore named ports are not supported for this field.

primary.description:
Make this the primary service (used in probes, notes, etc...).
If there is more than 1 service, make sure that only 1 service is marked as primary.

annotations.description: Annotations to add to the service account

create.description: Specifies whether a service account should be created

name.description:
The name of the service account to use.
If not set and create is true, a name is generated using the fullname template

serviceMonitor.description:
Configure the ServiceMonitors for the chart here.
Additional ServiceMonitors can be added by adding a dictionary key similar to the 'main' ServiceMonitors.

endpoints.description: Configures the endpoints for the serviceMonitor.

nameOverride.description: Override the name suffix that is used for this serviceMonitor.

selector.description:
Configures a custom selector for the serviceMonitor, this takes precedence over
specifying a service name.
Helm templates can be used.

serviceName.description: Configures the target Service for the serviceMonitor. Helm templates can be used.

sidecars.description:
Specify any sidecar containers here as dictionary items.
Each sidecar container should have its own key. The dictionary item key will determine the order.
Helm templates can be used.

topologySpreadConstraints.description:
Defines topologySpreadConstraint rules.
[[ref]](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-topology-spread-constraints/)
- maxSkew: <integer>
topologyKey: <string>
whenUnsatisfiable: <string>
labelSelector: <object>

volumeClaimTemplates.description:
Used in conjunction with `controller.type: statefulset` to create individual disks for each instance.
- name: data
labels: {}
annotations: {}
mountPath: /data
accessMode: "ReadWriteOnce"
size: 1Gi
- name: backup
labels: {}
annotations: {}
mountPath: /backup
subPath: theSubPath
accessMode: "ReadWriteOnce"
size: 2Gi
storageClass: cheap-storage-class
